summary: Carquinez Strait Light, Vallejo, California: a red light on a pier from January 1910 to 1951; its keepers' house was later moved to Glen Cove Marina.

lens.note: Smashed by vandals while the building waited to be moved after the 1955 sale (LighthouseFriends). The archive's record says 'Current Optic: REMOVED'.

fog_signal.type: duplicate compressed-air plant, two 6-inch automatic sirens
fog_signal.note: Described in the 1915 bulletin as in operation for more than a year; installation year not given.

structures.note: Pile driving began August 1908 (LighthouseFriends). A smaller beacon and fog signal were placed at the end of the extended pier in 1951. What remains is not described in the sources read.

structures.type: square frame tower attached to dwelling
structures.note: Not part of the building moved to Glen Cove Marina, which is 'minus its light tower and fog signal building' (LighthouseFriends). The sources read do not say what became of it.
Moved to Glen Cove Marina; the year of the move is not in these sources.
Automated beacon and fog signal at the end of the pier after 1951.

staffing.note: Coast Guard crew lived on the bluff after 1951; the last officer in charge left in summer 1963 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Glen Cove Marina reception area open to visitors; the upstairs rental is private (LighthouseFriends). The US Lighthouse Society lists the station as open to the public.

visit.note: Nothing lighthouse-related to see in the reception area (LighthouseFriends).

stay.note: Three-bedroom rental in the upper floors, opened 2014 (LighthouseFriends). Confirm availability with the operator.

facts.agency: Western Water Ways, Inc. (owner of the moved building, per LighthouseFriends)

corrections.why: The Twelfth District inspector's notice to mariners, printed in the San Francisco Call on 19 January 1910, gives 15 January 1910 as the date the light station was established. The 1908 in the record is the archive's 'Year Established'; LighthouseFriends dates the start of pile driving to August 1908.
The building moved to Glen Cove Marina is 'minus its light tower and fog signal building' (LighthouseFriends). The sources read do not say the tower survives anywhere.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive's place record gives 1908 as the year the station was established. The Twelfth District notice printed 19 January 1910 gives 15 January 1910 for the light station. Pile driving began in August 1908 (LighthouseFriends). The sources do not say why the archive's year differs.
The record gives the tower as built 1910 and LighthouseFriends says the dwelling, tower and fog building were completed near the end of 1909. The light was lit in January 1910.

notes_for_editor: Sources: LighthouseFriends (facts only; quotes kept short); the 19 January 1910 notice in the San Francisco Call, p. 15 (checked on the page image text; signed by the inspector of the Twelfth Lighthouse District, not the Lighthouse Board); Lighthouse Service Bulletins 1913, 1915 and 1921 (the 1913 and 1915 articles were checked against the page images: 1913 p. 39 gives 25 inches, 1915 p. 22 is the fog-signal article, which is the page that says the installation had been in successful operation for more than a year, and it is the article about Carquinez, not the breakwater light beside it); the Commissioner's report volume for 1915 to 1922 (the $6,749 line is under the heading for fiscal year 1922; the printed page 49 matches the page header in the text); the USLHS place record. Coordinates: the record's point is LighthouseFriends' Glen Cove Marina position (38.06781, -122.21372), where the building now stands; it is not the 1910 pier site. The USLHS place record gives 38 06.78 N, 122 21.38 W, about 13.5 km from that point; its latitude digits equal the LighthouseFriends decimal read as degrees and minutes, so it may be a transcription rather than a surveyed position. No location correction is proposed; the editor should decide. The USCG 1966 date for the lens lifting (quoted by Wikipedia) is not used. Wikipedia is not cited. The Carquinez Strait Light's range is given only as '13 miles' in the notice, with no unit, so no range_nm is set. The Coast Guard men and the keepers are named as the USLHS roster names them, with their span; the USLHS roster was matched by name to this station. Keepers Stanley V. Adler (1954-) and Thomas G. Lewis (1942-1957) overlap in the archive; LighthouseFriends does not list Adler. Hubert and the Western Water Ways owner are cited as published (LighthouseFriends), without further personal detail. Newspaper search for other 1908 to 1935 Carquinez items found only Notices to Mariners and bearing lists (SF Call 1911, 1912), not used.
